newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures yo-yo as market looks for lead.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures yo-yo as market looks for lead.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures continued to yo-yo within the day's range in afternoon trading on Friday as the market tried to find its feet amid downward pressure from NYMEX crude, dealers said.
March Brent traded 14 cents lower at $21.55 a barrel at 1629 GMT, up from the day's low of $21.50.
Brokers said the significant number for Brent was still support at $21.45 below which there was a gap on the spot continuation chart reaching to $21.
"Everyone is now trying to push it down to the lower levels, we've seen the higher levels and everyone's fed up of them," one broker said.
Some brokers said if Brent could hold support at $21.45 the market was likely to bounce back and see another rally.
More downward pressure on Brent came when NYMEX crude slipped through the $23 a barrel level for the first time in three months earlier on Friday afternoon.
But it soon bounced back above $23 so perpetuating the lack of direction felt in the London market over the last few days.
Feb gas oil remained stuck within its narrow range and traded $2.25 down at $189.50 a tonne.
The contract remained steady throughout the day having failed to push further down after breaking through support at $190.

The downturn was still attributed to technical factors but these were seen emphasised by the general bearish tone of the market, the milder weather in the United States and Europe and a surplus in world oil supplies.
"There has been no bullish news. The bullish news is gone, it's history...Yeltsin's alive, the weather's mild, so there's nothing fundamental to push it up," another said.
Some brokers said volume was light and was having difficulties moving anywhere. It was still waiting for the lead to come from NYMEX, they said.
